title: Unit Econ Dashboard — Metrics + Charts Brainstorm (working doc)
content:
Context
- We’re building an internal “unit economics” dashboard: blended cost of inference as $/1M output tokens, with drilldowns by model / region / customer tier.
- This doc is a scratchpad for: (a) which charts matter, (b) what questions execs/PMs/Eng will ask, (c) what data we need to answer those questions.
- Audience: Finance (FP&A), Product (Console/Hosted API/Optimize), Platform/Telemetry, SRE.

Non-goals (for MVP)
- Not a full billing/invoice UI.
- Not a per-customer profitability explorer (too sensitive + access control complexity).
- Not “perfect” causal attribution; we need “good enough to drive weekly decisions,” with clear caveats.

Canonical metric (we should put this on every chart)
- Blended cost per 1M output tokens (BC1M): $ / 1,000,000 output tokens
- “Blended” means: includes compute + allocated overhead per ADR-0142; we’ll need an explicit policy on discounts/credits inclusion for internal vs finance views.
- Primary default grain for the dashboard: daily (date) with filters.

Key workflows we expect
1) Weekly review: “Did unit cost go up/down WoW? What’s driving it?”
2) Regression detection: “We shipped a routing default / quant profile; did it move unit cost in prod?”
3) Mix shift awareness: “Our model mix / region mix changed; did that explain the movement?”
4) Optimization validation: “Did cache hit improve? Did that actually reduce compute per output token?”

Proposed top-level dashboard sections (MVP)
A) Executive summary
B) Trend + breakdown
C) Drilldown tables (top movers)
D) Cache + batching impact panel
E) “Explain delta” panel (driver attribution)

A) Executive summary (top of page)
Primary KPIs (big numbers, with delta vs prior period)
- BC1M (last 7d) + WoW delta
- Total output tokens (last 7d)
- Total blended cost (last 7d) — for tie-out sanity
- Gross margin proxy (optional; depends on discount/credits policy; may be finance-only)

Secondary KPIs (smaller)
- Weighted avg latency p50/p95 (context: are we trading cost for latency?)
- Cache hit rate (prefix and/or KV) and estimated cache savings
- % traffic on quantization profile(s) (if tag is available)

Open question: Do we show “blended cost (gross)” and “blended cost (net of discounts/credits)” as two toggles?
- Might be necessary because Product/Eng needs “true cost of serving,” Finance may need net view.
- Access control implications.

B) Trend + breakdown charts (the “money” section)
1) BC1M trend line (daily)
- Default: last 28 days
- Filters: model family/variant, region, tier
- Compare mode: vs prior period (previous 28d) or vs previous week

2) “Blended cost components” stacked area
- Y-axis: $/1M output tokens (same units as BC1M)
- Stack components (tentative):
  - Compute cost allocated to requests (GPU)
  - Non-GPU infra overhead allocation (network, storage, control-plane)
  - On-call / support allocation? (probably not; keep strictly infra COGS-ish)
  - Cache savings as a negative component (or show “compute before cache” and “compute after cache”)
- Goal: so the line goes up and the viewer immediately sees “it’s GPU rate, not overhead.”

3) BC1M by region (bar chart)
- Bar: current period BC1M by region
- Optional overlay: region share of tokens (to help interpret)
- Callouts: if region mapping changed, annotate.

4) BC1M by model (bar chart)
- Sort descending by BC1M or by token volume
- Important: allow “Top N models by output tokens” to avoid unreadable lists.
- Potential: group by model family (e.g., llama, mistral, qwen) then drill into variants.

C) Drilldown tables (actionable lists)
5) “Top movers” table (period-over-period)
- Rows: (model, region, tier) at a supported grain
- Columns:
  - BC1M current
  - BC1M previous
  - Delta $/1M
  - Output tokens current
  - Share of output tokens
  - Cache hit rate delta
  - Quant profile adoption delta
- Sort by “impact”: delta($/1M) * output_tokens_share (or approx cost impact $)

6) “Worst offenders” table (absolute)
- Rows: slices with highest BC1M above threshold token volume
- Used by Eng to target optimizations.

Open question: What’s the max cardinality we allow on this table without killing query latency?
- Suggest: only allow 2 of (model, region, tier) in one view for interactive queries; deeper combos via export job.

D) Cache + batching impact (optimization levers)
7) Cache metrics panel
- Prefix cache hit rate (if distinct) and KV cache hit rate
- Estimated cache savings ($/1M) or “compute tokens avoided”
- “Cache savings vs time” chart
- Consider splitting:
  - hit rate
  - savings estimate
  - “coverage” (% requests eligible for cache)

Notes
- Hit rate alone is misleading. A small increase in hit rate on long prompts might matter more.
- We likely need “saved prompt tokens” and “saved compute seconds” as intermediate metrics.

8) Batching / utilization proxy
- If we can get it: avg batch size, tokens/s/GPU, GPU utilization (or proxy: effective tokens/sec)
- These are very useful but risk being noisy or not comparable across model families.
- MVP might show: “effective throughput (output tokens per GPU-hour)” which maps more directly to cost.

E) “Explain delta” panel (driver attribution)
9) Explain BC1M change between two periods
Primary decomposition we can support with available dimensions:
- Region mix shift contribution
- Model mix shift contribution
- Tier mix shift contribution
- Within-slice cost change (e.g., same model+region+tier got more expensive)

Suggested UI output
- “BC1M increased by +$X/1M from Period A to Period B”
- Waterfall chart:
  - +$ from region mix
  - +$ from model mix
  - +$ from tier mix
  - +$ from within-slice cost changes
  - (optional) -$ from cache improvements
- Provide “Top 5 slices contributing to within-slice change” as a table.

Open questions (big ones)
1) Blended definition: credits/discounts
- Do we include promotional credits in “blended cost”?
  - Eng viewpoint: exclude (credits don’t change true cost)
  - Finance viewpoint: include in net margin reporting
- Proposal: compute two metrics in semantic layer:
  - bc1m_gross (exclude discounts/credits)
  - bc1m_net (include discounts/credits)
- Access control: net might be finance-only.

2) Overhead allocation method
- Flat $ allocation per output token? Per request? Per GPU-hour?
- Need to match ADR-0142 and FP&A expectations; must document.

3) Cost allocation correctness vs timeliness
- We need a freshness SLO, but accurate GPU allocation might require late-arriving fleet cost inputs.
- Idea: show “prelim” vs “finalized” partitions (e.g., last 48h flagged as provisional).

4) Mapping tables versioning
- Region mapping changes and tier mapping changes must be historically correct.
- Every chart needs an “as-of mapping version” to avoid “why did eu-west jump” confusion.

5) What to do with retries/fallbacks
- If routing falls back to a different model due to capacity, the cost might reflect the fallback.
- For product decisions we might want:
  - “requested_model” vs “served_model” breakdown
- MVP might only show served_model; add requested_model in V2.

6) Units and denominators
- Output tokens only vs total tokens (input+output)
- The project spec is $/1M output tokens, but we may also need $/1M total tokens for certain infra comparisons.

Rough layout sketch (text)

+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Filters: [Date range] [Region] [Tier] [Model] [Compare: prior period]           |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| BC1M (big)   | Output tokens (big) | Total blended cost (big) | Cache savings   |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| BC1M trend line (with compare)                                              |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Stacked area: cost components (compute, overhead, cache savings)              |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Bars: BC1M by region     | Bars: BC1M by model                                |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Table: Top movers (impact)                                                    |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Explain delta (waterfall + top contributors)                                   |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Cache panel (hit rate + savings over time) | Utilization proxy (optional)       |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Potential alert views (not sure if in MVP UI)
- “BC1M anomaly” alert: 7d rolling average up > X% WoW
- “Reconciliation variance” alert: dashboard totals vs billing totals > threshold
- “Freshness” alert: data delay > SLO

Notes from early stakeholder conversations
- Finance (Rishi): needs a stable weekly number + tie-out story more than perfect real-time.
- Product (Marissa): needs drilldown + shareable links for slices to discuss in rollout reviews.
- SRE (Allison/Aisha): wants explicit data health indicators (freshness/completeness) so we don’t page on phantom regressions.

Concrete next steps (for this doc)
- Convert chart list into a prioritized MVP list and map each chart -> required fields.
- Validate we can compute “cache savings estimate” reliably (or decide to defer).
- Agree on whether to surface “gross vs net” in UI and what RBAC applies.

Prioritized chart shortlist (current take)
P0 (must have)
- BC1M trend line + compare
- Components stacked area (compute vs overhead; cache savings optional)
- Bars: by region, by model
- Top movers table
- Data health indicator (freshness + reconciliation status)

P1 (nice)
- Explain delta waterfall
- Cache panel (hit rate + savings)
- Quant profile adoption overlay

P2 (later)
- requested_model vs served_model
- Throughput/utilization proxies
- Latency vs cost scatter (per model/region)

Appendix: questions we should be able to answer in <2 minutes using the dashboard
- “Why did BC1M jump last Tuesday?”
- “Is the jump concentrated in eu-west or global?”
- “Is it driven by model mix (more expensive models), or same model got worse?”
- “Did cache hit-rate drop? Did cache coverage change?”
- “Did a new quantization profile rollout reduce cost without moving latency?”
- “Can we reconcile the week’s blended cost to billing within tolerance?”
